humanTitle: People cannot see the player for the adverts covering it
whoItAffects: iPhone and Android users in the United Kingdom and the United States, across three app versions.

build.proposition: Keep the advert out of the surfaces a listener has to touch.
specifics: Never cover album art, the saved list, or search results
Put a floor under the gap between two audio adverts
State the frequency in the free tier’s own description
build.limitation: The free tier exists in order to be interrupted, so every change here trades against what pays for it.

start.proposition: Listening software whose free limits are published and then held.
specifics: One stated rate, changed only with notice
Aimed at people who will never pay but will stay for years
start.limitation: Music is licensed per play and the licence holders set the terms, so the software has little room to set them.

study.proposition: Where is the point at which interruption stops being tolerable?
specifics: Vary the spacing rather than the volume and see what people abandon
Separate the audio interruption from the visual one, which reviewers report apart
study.limitation: Advertising already studies tolerance, though rarely with the listener’s own account of it alongside.

write.proposition: Two songs, an advert, and then the album art disappears.
specifics: Set the frequency reviewers describe against what the tier promises
Quote the listener who sat and counted
write.limitation: Complaining about adverts is the oldest complaint there is, and only the count makes it reportable.
